title: 2021 Fall AMC 10A Problem 9
statement: When a certain unfair die is rolled, an even number is \(3\) times as likely to appear as an odd number. The die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers rolled is even?

solutions.text:
Let \(p\) be the probability that an odd number is rolled. Then \(3p\) is the probability an even number is rolled. We know that \[ p + 3p = 1 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{1}{4}. \]

The only way for the sum to be even is if both rolls have the same parity. This happens with a probability of \[ \dfrac{1}{4}^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}^2 = \dfrac{10}{16} = \dfrac{5}{8}. \]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Let the probability of odd be \(p,\) so even is \(3p\)
